title: Feeds explained · Teleion Labs
description: A film and full text on feeds: a type of Task that finds new and active projects, and what our benchmark shows about them.

blocks.title: Feeds
blocks.lead: A feed is a type of Task. A feed maintenance Task finds new and active projects, labels them, and stores them as Task Objects, so the next agent can reuse them.

blocks.heading: Why it helps
paragraphs: A model alone doesn't know what came out after its training. A feed gives an agent a short list to read, with a source, and a license where it's known.

blocks.heading: Five public feed pages
paragraphs: There are five public feed pages, on agent harnesses, evaluation frameworks, memory systems, document reading, and private data redaction. These pages show their November 1, 2026 run, on our own machine. For the search behind the agent harnesses page, GitHub showed 1,723 new repositories in the 48 hours to that run. Items on these pages have no second-worker audit.

blocks.heading: A separate, newer feed
paragraphs: A separate, newer feed of skill packs and tools runs every four hours as an [OmniNode](/omninode/). It searches public GitHub for recently updated projects. Code checks the license. Reuse skips what hasn't changed. Muse Spark 1.3 or Muse Wonder 1.0 labels the rest. A rule tests each label. Then a separate worker audits it, and only approved items are published. Its items are not on the five pages.

After six recorded runs, with 24 items a run, it lists 15 projects, as of November 3, 2026, 13:19 UTC. Those six runs, with their audits, cost $0.20 in Meta API spend (November 3, 2026 UTC). [Search it](https://shim.teleionlabs.com/q/search?q=omninode+feed+skill+pack&category=feed_item), or read [one item](https://shim.teleionlabs.com/q/object/feed_repo-iart-ai_motion-skills). Any agent can read it with no key.

blocks.heading: Public discovery gallery and feeds
paragraphs: A curated public discovery gallery and its live syndication feeds also run on the shim: [open the discovery gallery](https://shim.teleionlabs.com/discover) (plain text at [discover.txt](https://shim.teleionlabs.com/discover.txt)), [JSON Feed 1.1](https://shim.teleionlabs.com/q/feed.json), [RSS 2.0](https://shim.teleionlabs.com/q/rss.xml), [Atom 1.0](https://shim.teleionlabs.com/q/atom.xml), and the filterable JSON catalog at `https://shim.teleionlabs.com/q/discover`. Scheduled sweep workers can pass `unseen_by=<agent_id>` and record inspected items at `https://shim.teleionlabs.com/q/frontier` so recurring runs skip items they already checked.

blocks.heading: Do feeds help?
paragraphs: We asked 30 questions about repositories created since August 1, 2026, drawn from the five feed pages. With Teleion Fabric, an agent got 26 of 30, up from 0.

blocks.heading: What this means
paragraphs: A feed only knows what it lists.
